acquisitionPaths.uploadProtocol: Presigned S3 PUT per part (600s). Optional client x-amz-checksum-sha256 is signed into the URL. A resumable S3 multipart fork via /v1/uploads/sessions applies when the flag is on and the file is large.
acquisitionPaths.clientHash: Sent as checksumSha256Base64 and clientSignals.clientHintSha256Base64. Used only as the S3 upload precondition and a stored hint, never persisted as authority.
acquisitionPaths.serverHash: completeEvidence streams each part version from S3 into sha256HexFromStream (evidence-complete.service.ts:768-769). For multipart, fileSha256 = sha256 of the part hashes joined by '|', plus a manifest sha256.
acquisitionPaths.metadata: Client-supplied: type, mimeType, names, deviceTimeIso, gps, intakePlanJson, internalNotes, tz/locale. Server-derived: capturedAtUtc, S3 content-type and size.
acquisitionPaths.custody: In the create tx: EVIDENCE_CREATED, IDENTITY_SNAPSHOT_RECORDED, UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED. In the complete tx: UPLOAD_COMPLETED, SIGNATURE_APPLIED, TIMESTAMP_APPLIED/FAILED. After commit: EVIDENCE_LOCKED or STORAGE_PROTECTION_UNAVAILABLE. EVIDENCE_COMPLETED is best-effort at the route.
acquisitionPaths.jobs: automation EVIDENCE_CREATED (in tx), webhook evidence.created, OTS anchoring, report generation when funded, webhook evidence.completed, malware scan, finalization fanout, graph reconcile
acquisitionPaths.idempotency: create: none (no idempotency key; a retry makes a new row). parts: idempotent on (evidenceId, partIndex) under an advisory lock; returns a fresh PUT URL. complete: advisory lock, SIGNED early return, and an updateMany claim CREATED|UPLOADING->SIGNED (evidence-complete.service.ts:1098-1104).

answers.question: Is client-supplied sha256 trusted as authority?
answers.answer: Not on the web or intake presign paths. The client checksum only signs the S3 PUT precondition. fileSha256 is recomputed on the server from the stored object version at completion.

evidence.snippet: const sha256 = await sha256HexFromStream(body as unknown as Readable);

answers.question: Can finalize be run twice?
answers.answer: No. Finalize holds an advisory lock, returns early on SIGNED, and claims the row with an updateMany limited to CREATED|UPLOADING. FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH is refused with 409. The fire-once side effects after commit are a separate problem (see ACQ-03).

answers.question: What is the scope and lifetime of a presigned URL?
answers.answer: The server builds the key from the evidence id (evidence/<id>/...) and sanitizes the filename. The URL is valid for 600s and ContentType is signed. Content-Length is not signed, so the size limit is only enforced after the object has been hashed (ACQ-04).

answers.question: Does every Evidence creation write a custody event?
answers.answer: Yes. The single creator writes EVIDENCE_CREATED, IDENTITY_SNAPSHOT_RECORDED and UPLOAD_AUTHORIZED in the same transaction as the insert. The seed scripts are the exception (ACQ-9).

answers.question: Can a caller-supplied teamId create Evidence without membership proof?
answers.answer: No foreign workspace: createEvidence requires an ACTIVE TeamMember row and returns 403 otherwise. But membership status is the only check. Role, access expiry and org lifecycle are not evaluated (ACQ-01).

findings.title: POST /v1/evidence authorizes by membership status only, so VIEWERs, members with expired access and members of SUSPENDED orgs can create workspace Evidence
findings.observed: createEvidence accepts any ACTIVE TeamMember row for the caller-supplied teamId. It never runs evaluateMemberAccess or authorizeOrFail with evidence.create, so role, accessExpiresAtUtc and organization status are all ignored. The direct-capture door does run authorizeOrFail (capture-trust.routes.ts:711). The same bug was fixed for POST /v1/cases (plan-matrix test p7.team.direct_api.ui_locked_action_denied) but not for this route.
findings.expected: Creation should go through the canonical evidence.create decision for the target workspace.
findings.dataFlow: body.teamId -> createEvidence -> teamMember status check -> tx.evidence.create + custody + automation trigger + webhook
findings.rootCause: createEvidence uses a hand-rolled membership check instead of the canonical access engine.
findings.blastRadius: Every workspace that has VIEWER members, time-boxed members, or a suspended parent org.
findings.impact: A VIEWER can create UPLOADING rows, custody events, automation runs and evidence.created webhooks. Those rows use up the TEAM rolling cap, and the viewer can PUT bytes to the root presigned URL. Completion is refused because parts and complete need evidence.update_metadata, so the rows stay orphaned permanently.
findings.reproduction: Seed a TEAM workspace with a VIEWER member. POST /v1/evidence {type:'PHOTO', teamId} using the VIEWER's token. The expected answer is 403; the actual answer is 201.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Copy plan-matrix p7.team.direct_api.ui_locked_action_denied, point it at POST /v1/evidence, and assert with the denyWithoutSideEffects fingerprint.
findings.remediation: For non-personal captures, have createEvidence call evaluateMemberAccess with permission evidence.create, or have the route call authorizeOrFail first.
findings.acceptanceProof: VIEWER, expired-access and suspended-org requests get 403 and leave zero evidence, custody or automation rows.
findings.migrationBackfill: optional: find UPLOADING rows whose owner lacked evidence.create

findings.title: Interrupted web captures leave Evidence in UPLOADING permanently; these rows count against record caps and are never reaped

evidence.snippet: return db.evidence.count({ where: { ownerUserId, deletedAt: null, lifecycleState: { not: "DESTROYED" },
// Read-only first pass. ... NO destructive action is taken.

findings.observed: The web client creates the Evidence row before any bytes are uploaded. If a part presign or PUT fails, the client throws and the row stays UPLOADING. A retry creates a new row. The cap counts include rows in every status, and orphan-scan only logs counts.
findings.expected: Abandoned reservations should not use up plan capacity, and they should be reaped or resumed.
findings.dataFlow: create row -> upload fails -> row stays UPLOADING -> retry creates a new row -> cap counts both
findings.rootCause: The row is reserved before upload, the cap predicate ignores status, and nothing reaps stale rows.
findings.blastRadius: All web captures. FREE has a lifetime cap of 3.
findings.impact: A FREE user with a few failed uploads is refused new records while holding no signed evidence.
findings.reproduction: As a FREE user, create 3 records via POST /v1/evidence without completing them. The 4th POST returns 409 FREE_LIMIT_REACHED.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration test running the reproduction above.
findings.remediation: Count only finalized rows, or reuse the UPLOADING row on retry. Add a reaper that closes stale reservations with a custody event.
findings.acceptanceProof: The 4th capture is admitted, and the reaper closes stale rows with custody events.
findings.migrationBackfill: optional cleanup of stale UPLOADING rows
findings.ownerDecision: Should abandoned reservations count toward caps?

findings.title: Malware scan, the evidence.completed webhook and finalization fanout fire once after commit; a retention or lock-snapshot failure or a crash skips them permanently

evidence.snippet: await enqueueScan({ evidenceId: ev.id, teamId: ev.teamId! });

findings.observed: The SIGNED status is committed first. If retention or the lock snapshot then throws, everything after it is skipped. A retry takes the alreadyFinalized path, which re-requests OTS and the report but returns before the webhook, scan and fanout. grep shows enqueueScan and runEvidenceFinalizationFanout each have exactly one caller.
findings.expected: These side effects should be durable (an outbox) or re-driven when the record is already finalized.
findings.dataFlow: commit SIGNED -> retention throws -> 500 -> retry -> alreadyFinalized early return
findings.rootCause: Fire-once work runs after the commit with no outbox.
findings.blastRadius: Every completion that hits a transient Object Lock or HEAD failure, or a crash in that window.
findings.impact: A signed original is never malware-scanned or indexed, and no evidence.completed webhook is sent.
findings.reproduction: Make PutObjectRetention fail once, then call complete twice. No scan row is ever created.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration test with a storage double whose retention call fails the first time.
findings.remediation: Write outbox rows inside the finalize transaction, or run these side effects idempotently on the alreadyFinalized path.
findings.acceptanceProof: After the retry, a scan row and a fanout exist.
findings.migrationBackfill: Enqueue scans for SIGNED evidence that has no scan record.

findings.title: The size limit is checked only after every part has been streamed and hashed inside a 120s interactive DB transaction, and the presigned PUT does not limit Content-Length
findings.observed: Every part is downloaded and hashed before the total is compared with MAX_EVIDENCE_SIZE (default 1 GiB). Hashing, signing and the TSA call all run inside the transaction.
findings.expected: Reject oversize uploads using the HEAD sizes first, and hash outside the interactive transaction.
findings.dataFlow: PUT of any size -> complete -> full stream -> timeout or 413
findings.rootCause: The size check runs after the streaming loop, and the I/O runs inside the DB transaction.
findings.impact: A large legitimate upload can time out on every attempt and stay UPLOADING. Oversize uploads waste server bandwidth and DB connections.
findings.reproduction: Upload about 1 GiB over a throttled S3 connection and call complete.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Latency rig with a throttled storage double.
findings.remediation: Sum the HEAD sizes before streaming, and hash before the transaction, bound to versionId.
findings.acceptanceProof: An oversize upload gets 413 without any GET, and a large upload completes.

findings.title: The required-checklist gate enforces a plan the client wrote (intakePlanJson), and the template identity stamp does not check who owns the capture session

findings.observed: A raw API caller can omit intakePlanJson, which skips the checklist gate, while templateSlug is still copied from any captureSessionId without an owner check.
findings.expected: Required steps come from the template on the server side, and the session lookup is scoped to its owner.
findings.rootCause: The server trusts the client's plan.
findings.blastRadius: Template captures made through the raw API.
findings.impact: A record can carry a template identity without meeting that template's required steps.
findings.reproduction: POST /v1/evidence with a template draft's captureSessionId and no plan, then complete it with one part. It is accepted.
findings.runtimeProofIdea: Integration test running the reproduction above.
findings.remediation: Derive the required steps from the template row, and filter the session lookup by owner.
findings.ownerDecision: Is checklist completion a product guarantee?

findings.title: The record-cap count is read without a lock, and SHARED workspaces are not re-checked at completion
findings.observed: Concurrent creates at cap-1 all pass. Personal records are settled again under a lock at completion; SHARED records are not.
findings.impact: The contracted monthly cap can be exceeded by a small margin.
findings.remediation: Lock the capacity subject for SHARED workspaces too.

findings.title: POST /v1/evidence/:id/parts has no upper bound on partIndex, no cap on part count, and no rate limit
findings.observed: The owner can create any number of part rows and presigned URLs. Gaps and out-of-order indexes are accepted, and completion seals whatever parts exist.
findings.expected: The number of parts should be bounded.
findings.remediation: Add a maximum part count and a rate limit.

questions.q: PutObjectRetention and the lock-snapshot HEAD use the key without a versionId, while the hash is bound to storageVersionId. The presigned PUT also sets ObjectLock headers, so each version is locked when written. Is the bucket's default retention guaranteed? If not, a PUT to a still-valid URL after hashing would make the lock snapshot describe a different version than the one that was hashed.
The route appends EVIDENCE_COMPLETED custody after commit as best-effort and never appends it again on retry. Does chain verification tolerate the event being missing?
Can production reach the seed scripts that insert Evidence directly with no custody (for example through ops-seed.routes.ts)?
